solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Against army regulation for poisonous stuff

blocks.note: anti means against
AR is the abbreviation for army regulation

explanation.surface: Someone objects that some toxic material breaches military rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiar is the poisonous latex of the upas tree, once used to tip arrows in Java.

clue.text: Absolute leader in Turkey, say imprisoning a bishop?

definitions.text: Absolute leader in Turkey, say imprisoning a bishop?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
to imprison is to shut something inside, so one group of letters goes within another

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for absolute, as in absolute temperature
the first letter of Turkey
taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
e.g. means for example, that is, say

explanation.surface: A question whether a powerful Turkish ruler might, for instance, lock up a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: T and EG wrap round A B, with the A for absolute in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An atabeg was a hereditary governor or ruling prince under the Seljuk Turks, effectively an autocrat.

clue.text: Bill and penniless partners making tunics for ladies

indicators.note: having no pennies means losing the letter that stands for a penny

blocks.note: a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab
pards is slang for partners or pals

explanation.surface: An invoice and some broke business associates lead to a line of women's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the abbreviation for penny, so PARDS loses its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a sleeveless tunic, and Chambers notes it as a woman's sleeveless jacket or overgarment.

clue.text: Queen shown up on front of metal clasp

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept
in a down clue showing something up means writing it from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: the first letter of metal
a rani is an Indian queen

explanation.surface: A queen appears wearing a metal brooch or fastening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' here puts the queen after the M before the whole lot is turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Inarm is a poetic verb meaning to embrace, to hold in the arms, which is to clasp.

clue.text: Test is shortened in Australian state

indicators.note: shortened tells us to use the clipped form of the word, which then sits within the rest
in places one piece inside the others

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for Australian
is shortened becomes the 's of contractions
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A cricket Test match is cut short in one of Australia's states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Australian state' reads as one phrase but splits into A and a verb meaning declare.
explanation.definitionFit: An assay is a test or analysis, especially of a metal's purity.

clue.text: Horse down under Midlands city in reserve

blocks.note: Brum is the nickname for Birmingham, the big city of the English Midlands
kept by, as in putting something by for later

explanation.surface: An Australian horse is held back in reserve in Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: A brumby is a wild or feral horse of the Australian outback; down under means Australia.

clue.text: Head of Balliol departs in lots of wet weather — a loss of talent

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
in sets one piece inside another

blocks.note: the first letter of Balliol, an Oxford college
plenty of downpour, the word for it doubled
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: An Oxford college master leaves in a downpour, and the university loses its talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots of' asks for the weather word twice, with D slipped between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain drain is the emigration of skilled or clever people, a loss of talent to elsewhere.

clue.text: Early drive from perch catch on Stour

indicators.note: a catch is a round sung by voices, so the letters go round into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; the Stour is an English river

explanation.surface: An angler on the river Stour scares birds off their perch at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early' marks an obsolete word rather than a time of day.
explanation.definitionFit: To unroost is an old verb for driving a bird off its roost, a roost being a perch.

clue.text: Most buxom couples in sculpture

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: a bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders
ties is a verb meaning couples or links

explanation.surface: The most voluptuous pairs of figures are found in a sculpture group.
explanation.definitionFit: Busty means large-breasted, so the superlative describes the most buxom figure.

clue.text: Positive responses from the old-fashioned session served up

indicators.note: in a down clue something served up is written bottom to top

blocks.note: ye is the archaic spelling of the
sess is the abbreviation for session

explanation.surface: Favourable replies come out of an old-style meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the session abbreviation is turned up; the archaic article stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesses is the plural of yes used as a noun: affirmative answers or votes.

clue.text: Customs document isn't rare when travelling

indicators.note: travelling moves things about, so the letters move into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Customs paperwork is common enough when you go abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A transire is a customs warrant letting coastwise goods pass from one port to another.

clue.text: Outmoded couple in pieces head for geriatrician

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: chess pieces are called men
the first letter of geriatrician

explanation.surface: An elderly pair falls apart and is sent to a doctor for the old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outmoded' marks an obsolete word; the old couple are not the definition's people at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Meng is an obsolete verb meaning to mix or join together, so to couple.

clue.text: Dope imported by nameless Chinese official, smooth agent

indicators.note: without a name means the letter standing for name is dropped
something imported is brought inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: an amban was a Chinese imperial official in a dependency such as Tibet
a dope is a fool, an ass
to dress stone or timber is to smooth it

explanation.surface: A slick operative smuggles drugs in via an anonymous Chinese functionary.
explanation.walkthrough: N for name goes from the official's title, then the fool sits inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassadress is a female ambassador, a diplomatic agent representing her state.

clue.text: Consider soldier in two ways for military planner

indicators.note: in sets the first pieces inside the others

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way, taken twice
to rate is to consider or reckon
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A general weighs up a soldier from two angles before committing troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategist plans the overall conduct of a war or campaign, a military planner.

clue.text: Arab cuts dodgy habit concerning Indian republic

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are not in their proper order
something that cuts into a word goes inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
AR is the abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: An Arab gives up a shady habit with regard to India.
explanation.definitionFit: Bharat is the Hindi name of India, and Bharati is the adjective relating to it.

clue.text: One disallowed tips in Cape ferry-boats?

indicators.note: what is disallowed is not permitted to stay, so it is removed

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
points are tips, as of pencils

explanation.surface: A tipster is barred, perhaps, from betting on ferries at the Cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape' is the Cape of South Africa, where pont is the word for a river ferry.
explanation.definitionFit: In South Africa a pont is a flat-bottomed ferry boat, often pulled across by cable.

clue.text: As before dump plans hardly to be believed

blocks.note: a lay is a plan or scheme, as in the lay of the land
tall as in a tall story

explanation.surface: Plans for a waste tip are as incredible as ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks an archaic word and belongs with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A laystall is an old word for a place where rubbish and dung were laid, a refuse heap.

clue.text: Scotland's happy, Gove about to embrace independence

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters are rearranged
to embrace is to hold something in the arms, so one letter sits inside the rest

blocks.note: taken as written; Michael Gove is a Scottish-born Conservative politician
I is the abbreviation for independence or independent

explanation.surface: A Scottish politician is said to be pleased about embracing independence for Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Vogie is a Scots adjective meaning merry, cheerful or proud.

clue.text: Asian dish good anonymous party made twice

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
A is the abbreviation for anonymous
a do is a party
the three pieces so far are repeated

explanation.surface: A tasty Asian meal served at a secret gathering, cooked a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Gado-gado is an Indonesian salad of vegetables with peanut sauce.

clue.text: Work on a course of gems

blocks.note: op. is the abbreviation for opus, a work
'on' places the work first; a line is a course or route

explanation.surface: A jeweller studies a training course on precious stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaline means like opal, the iridescent gemstone, so it describes a quality of gems.

clue.text: Foot soldier rested in enclosure

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the second

blocks.note: a hope is a small enclosed valley
lit means alighted or settled, as a bird rests on a branch

explanation.surface: An infantryman took a break inside a stockade.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoplite was a heavily armed infantryman of ancient Greece, a foot soldier.

clue.text: Consume endless freshwater fish

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter

blocks.note: to discuss a meal or bottle is a jocular way to say consume it

explanation.surface: Someone eats an unending supply of river fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The discus is a disc-shaped South American cichlid, a popular freshwater aquarium fish.

clue.text: Wild asters screening tip, mostly in layers

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes
wild means uncontrolled, so the letters run out of order
to screen something is to hide it behind or within, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
the tip is the top

explanation.surface: Wild flowers are shielding a heap of something stacked in strata.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratose is a botanical term meaning arranged in strata, that is, layered.

clue.text: At the very moment when hospital lady turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a san is a sanatorium, a hospital
Eve, the first lady

explanation.surface: A woman arrives at a hospital just in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Even as is a conjunction meaning just when, at exactly the time that something happens.

clue.text: Scottish island's independent butcher

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for independent
to butcher is to slaughter, to slay

explanation.surface: A Hebridean island has its own self-employed meat trader.
explanation.definitionFit: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides, off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: House can set about conclusion of Brexit

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter
something set about another is placed around it

blocks.note: can and loo are both slang for a toilet
the final letter of Brexit

explanation.surface: Parliament's chamber could be arranged around the end of Brexit.
explanation.walkthrough: House is the bingo game, also called housey-housey, not a building or a chamber of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Loto is a variant spelling of lotto, the numbers game also known as house.

clue.text: Poison not for all to see in trading vessel

indicators.note: not means without, so the following letter is taken away

blocks.note: curare is an arrow poison from South America
U is the film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: Toxic cargo is hidden from public view aboard a merchant ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A crare, or crayer, was a small trading ship of earlier centuries.

clue.text: Foremost of Brexiteers (originally Remainer) is me

definitions.text: Foremost of Brexiteers (originally Remainer) is me

indicators.note: the foremost part of each word is its first letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: the first letters of these three words
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician boasts of leading the Leave campaign despite starting out on the Remain side.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, spoken by Boris Johnson, who led Vote Leave in 2016 after famously drafting a column for each side.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson was the best-known figurehead of the Brexit campaign, so 'me' in his mouth identifies him.

clue.text: English poet's nipped north with a great deal on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is back to front, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for north
lots means a great deal

explanation.surface: An English poet pinched a large amount from the north, thinking it over later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English poet's' means a form used by a poet such as Milton or Spenser; nipped is slang for stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoln is an old poetic contraction of stolen, and to nip is informal for to steal.

clue.text: Mushroom bap for tea initially in French farmhouse

indicators.note: one thing given for another means it is swapped in, replacing it
initially points to the first letter only

blocks.note: a gîte is a French country cottage or farmhouse let to holidaymakers
the first letter of tea
a bap is a soft bread roll

explanation.surface: Someone eats a bread roll rather than tea at a French holiday farmhouse, with mushrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The roll replaces the T in the farmhouse word. A bap is a British soft bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: The girolle is the chanterelle, a yellow edible mushroom prized in French cooking.

clue.text: Model in Italian car associated with daring design

indicators.note: to model is to shape or fashion, so the letters are moulded anew

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashion model poses in an Italian sports car with a bold, striking look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun for the person in the car, but it is a verb telling us to reshape the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Catilinarian refers to Catiline, whose audacious plot to overthrow Rome was exposed by Cicero; a design here is a scheme.

clue.text: Russian VIP excited finally with leader sacked on return

indicators.note: a leader sacked is removed from the front, so the opening letter goes
returning means going back, so the letters are read in reverse order

blocks.note: astir means in a state of excitement or bustle
last means finally, as in at last

explanation.surface: An important Russian gets agitated at last after their party head is fired on returning home.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsaritsa was a Russian empress or the wife of a tsar, a very important person.

clue.text: Most knowing remains found in Sao Tome

indicators.note: found in places the first word inside the second

blocks.note: ST is the international code for São Tomé and Príncipe
something that lies there remains in place

explanation.surface: Wise archaeologists unearth remains on the African island of São Tomé.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a noun for relics, but it is a verb meaning stays.
explanation.definitionFit: Sly means cunning or shrewd, so the slyest person is the most knowing.

clue.text: Origin in Latin seems wrong for lepers of yore

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, its first letter
wrong means not right, so the letters are out of their correct order

blocks.note: the first letter of Latin
taken as written

explanation.surface: A word's Latin root appears mistaken when applied to people with leprosy in olden days.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesel is an obsolete word for a leper, from Old French via Latin misellus, wretched.
